FIAT_SHAMIR_MODEL.md:88 and this port say that they are selected. The proof is not affected, but the headers mislead an auditor about which verifier the target covers.

target.Holds builds the narrow Lifecycle.setup, whose nifs field uses ProductionKey.key. RecursiveTerminalTransition reads only setup.verifierKeys (Spec/HyperNova/Construction2/Paper.lean:557-595), so the narrow NIFS field has no effect. The wide key enters only through the relation rows and OpeningBinding.terminal_implies_stepOrCollision (Wide/TerminalSecurity.lean:168). No soundness effect.

No theorem references Wide.selected. The target covers it only through universal quantification over Wide.Target. Only executables obtain a Compiled value (compile? has no Lean proof that it returns some), and parts is a free argument. The claim that the Rust package's verifier is target.Holds for Wide.selected belongs to P.binding.context and P.delivery.terminal, not to this obligation.

The history witnesses are arbitrary-length List F, and the approved hash-chain step accepts any message length. Thus 'no valid history' also counts histories with messages that are not circuit width as valid. This follows the HyperNova IVC definition relative to F = program.step. It is unchanged from the old target.
